entries.name: Isolated DC-to-DC converter
entries.summary: A DC/DC converter with an internal high-frequency transformer that separates input and output galvanically.
description: An isolated DC/DC converter uses a high-frequency transformer between its input and output stages, so the two DC systems have no conductive connection. Isolation lets the output be earthed differently from the input, for example a floating battery bus supplying an earthed control system, or keeps a fault on one side from reaching the other.
Drawings show the DC/DC box with a transformer mark or a pair of coupled coils inside, or a vertical double line across the box. The isolation voltage is a key rating and should be written beside it.

The symbol alone does not state the test voltage or whether the isolation is functional or reinforced for safety. Those properties decide whether the output can be treated as a separated circuit, so they must be read from the product data.
readingNotes: A transformer mark inside the box shows isolation.
Read the isolation rating rather than assuming safety separation.
drawingChecklist: State input and output voltages and isolation voltage.
Show earthing on each side.
Reference isolation class.
entries.distinction: An isolated converter separates input and output; a non-isolated buck or boost converter shares a common conductor.

facts.label: Earthing
facts.value: Each side can be earthed independently

entries.name: Static frequency converter
entries.summary: A rectifier and inverter in one unit that converts AC at one frequency to AC at another, such as 50 Hz to 60 Hz.
description: A static frequency converter rectifies the incoming AC to DC and inverts it back to AC at a different frequency and often a different voltage. It is used to supply 60 Hz equipment from a 50 Hz network, to provide shore power to ships, to feed 400 Hz aircraft supplies and to link microgrids or networks running at different frequencies.

Drawings show a converter box with AC marks on both sides and the frequencies noted, or two converter boxes back to back with a DC link between them. Input and output transformers are often drawn to provide isolation and voltage matching.

The output is converter-sourced, so fault current is limited and selective protection downstream must be checked. The symbol does not show overload capability or whether the output can supply motor starting current.
readingNotes: Read both the input and output frequency labels.
Check output short-circuit capability for downstream protection.
drawingChecklist: State input and output voltage and frequency.
Show isolation transformers.
Reference overload and fault capability.
entries.distinction: A static frequency converter changes frequency electronically; a motor-generator set does the same with rotating machines.

entries.name: Motor-generator set
entries.summary: A motor mechanically coupled to a generator, used to isolate, change frequency or convert between AC and DC.
description: A motor-generator set is an electric motor driving a generator on a common shaft. It provides complete electrical isolation, conversion of frequency or voltage, or AC to DC conversion, and its rotating mass rides through short disturbances. Some sets add a flywheel or an engine on the same shaft for backup.

Drawings show two machine circles, one marked M and one marked G, joined by a mechanical coupling line. The motor input and generator output are on separate circuits, each with its own protection and earthing.

Efficiency is lower than a static converter and the rotating machines need maintenance, so motor-generator sets are now mainly found in legacy, test or special-purpose installations. The symbol does not show speed, coupling arrangement or ride-through time.
readingNotes: The coupling line shows a mechanical link, not an electrical one.
Earthing of the generator output is independent of the motor supply.
drawingChecklist: State motor and generator ratings.
Show output earthing and protection.
Reference flywheel or engine if fitted.
entries.distinction: A motor-generator set converts through rotating machines; a static frequency converter uses power electronics.

entries.name: Static transfer switch
entries.summary: A thyristor-based switch that transfers a load between two synchronised sources within a quarter cycle.
description: A static transfer switch uses back-to-back thyristor pairs on each of two sources to move a critical load from one supply to the other in a few milliseconds. It is used in data centres and process plants, typically downstream of two UPS systems, so that a failure in one UPS or its distribution does not interrupt the load.

The single-line diagram shows two incoming feeders, each passing through an anti-parallel thyristor symbol or a solid-state switch box, joining at a common output. Mechanical bypass switches for maintenance are drawn in parallel with the static paths.

Fast transfer only works when the two sources are close in phase. The symbol does not show the synchronisation window, the transfer inhibit logic on downstream faults or how transformer inrush is managed when the load includes transformers.
readingNotes: Look for bypass switches around each thyristor path.
Transfer is normally blocked for downstream faults; check the logic.
drawingChecklist: State current rating and transfer time.
Show both sources and maintenance bypasses.
Reference synchronisation and inhibit logic.
entries.distinction: A static transfer switch uses thyristors and transfers in milliseconds; an automatic transfer switch uses mechanical contacts and takes much longer.

entries.name: Automatic transfer switch
entries.summary: A mechanically switched changeover device that automatically moves a load from a failed normal source to an alternate source.
description: An automatic transfer switch monitors the normal supply and, when voltage or frequency goes out of limits, signals the generator to start and transfers the load to the alternate source once it is ready. When the normal supply returns and is stable, it transfers back after a time delay. Most units use an open-transition break-before-make sequence.

Single-line diagrams show a changeover contact with two incoming poles labelled N and E or S1 and S2 and one outgoing load connection, or two interlocked switching devices. The controller and generator start signal are often noted beside it, and a neutral pole may be switched for separately derived systems.

The symbol does not show the timing, whether the neutral is switched, or whether the transition is open, closed or delayed. Those features determine earthing behaviour, motor reconnection and coordination with the network operator.
readingNotes: Check whether three or four poles are switched.
Read the transition type from the notes.
drawingChecklist: State current rating, poles and transition type.
Show both sources and the generator start signal.
Reference controller timing settings.
entries.distinction: An automatic transfer switch operates without an operator; a manual transfer switch needs someone to move it.

entries.name: Manual transfer switch
entries.summary: An operator-moved changeover switch that selects which of two sources supplies a load, with an off position between them.
description: A manual transfer switch is a changeover switch operated by hand, usually with three positions: source 1, off and source 2. It is common where a portable or small standby generator connects through an inlet, and as a maintenance or bypass switch in larger systems where automatic transfer is not required.

The drawing is a changeover contact with a manual operator mark, often labelled I-0-II, with the two sources above and the load below. The mechanical design prevents both sources being connected at once.

The symbol does not tell you whether the switch can be operated on load, or whether the neutral is switched. Operating procedures, including starting the generator before moving the switch, belong in the operating instructions.
readingNotes: The off position between sources is part of the safety function.
Check whether the switch is rated for on-load operation.
drawingChecklist: State rating, poles and positions.
Show the generator inlet or second source.
Reference operating procedure.
entries.distinction: A manual transfer switch relies on an operator; an automatic transfer switch senses source failure and acts on its own.

entries.name: Closed-transition transfer switch
entries.summary: A transfer switch that briefly parallels two synchronised sources so the load moves without interruption.
description: A closed-transition transfer switch connects the load to the new source before disconnecting it from the old one, with both sources paralleled for a short time, typically less than 100 milliseconds. A synchronism check confirms that voltage, frequency and phase angle are within limits before the overlap is allowed.

Drawings show two switching devices or a transfer switch with both contacts able to close, plus a synchronism check function and often a note on maximum overlap time. Where the overlap is longer than the network operator allows, a soft-load transfer with a paralleling controller is used instead.

Even a momentary parallel connection can require approval from the network operator and protection against the generator feeding a utility fault. The symbol does not show the overlap timer, its backup trip or the interface protection.
readingNotes: A synchronism check function should be associated with the switch.
Read the maximum overlap time permitted.
drawingChecklist: State overlap time and synchronising limits.
Show synchronism check and backup trip.
Reference network operator approval.
entries.distinction: A closed-transition switch overlaps the two sources; an open-transition switch always breaks before it makes.

entries.name: Bypass-isolation transfer switch
entries.summary: An automatic transfer switch paired with a manual bypass switch so the ATS can be isolated for maintenance without losing the load.
description: A bypass-isolation transfer switch combines an automatic transfer switch with a parallel manual bypass switch. The bypass can connect the load directly to either source while the automatic switch is withdrawn or isolated, so maintenance and testing can proceed without interrupting critical loads such as hospital or emergency circuits.

Single-line diagrams draw the automatic changeover in one path and a manually operated changeover in parallel, with isolating contacts on the automatic unit. Interlocks prevent the bypass from connecting the load to a source different from the one the automatic switch is using at the moment of bypass.
The symbol does not show the interlock sequence or whether the bypass operation is load-break. Operators need the switching procedure to use it safely.
readingNotes: Identify the isolating contacts that allow the automatic unit to be withdrawn.
Bypass and automatic paths should be interlocked.
drawingChecklist: State ratings for both paths.
Show isolation contacts and interlocks.
Reference bypass procedure.
entries.distinction: A bypass-isolation switch adds a manual path around the ATS; a plain ATS must be de-energised for maintenance.

entries.name: Online double-conversion UPS
entries.summary: A UPS whose rectifier and inverter carry the load continuously, with the battery on the DC link and a static bypass.
description: In an online double-conversion UPS the load is always supplied by the inverter. The rectifier converts incoming AC to DC, the battery floats on the DC link, and the inverter produces a regulated output that is independent of input voltage and frequency variations. When the input fails, the battery simply takes over the DC link with no transfer.

Single-line diagrams show rectifier and inverter blocks in series with the battery connected between them, a static bypass switch in parallel, and often a separate bypass input and an external maintenance bypass. Output isolation transformers may also be shown.

The double-conversion path costs a few per cent in efficiency and some units offer an eco mode that runs on bypass, which changes the protection the load actually receives. The symbol does not show which mode is set, battery autonomy or the bypass source arrangement.
readingNotes: Look for separate rectifier and bypass inputs; they may come from different boards.
Check whether eco mode is enabled.
drawingChecklist: State kVA, kW and battery autonomy.
Show static bypass and maintenance bypass.
Reference operating mode.
entries.distinction: An online UPS powers the load through the inverter all the time; a line-interactive UPS passes mains to the load and only inverts during disturbances.

entries.name: Line-interactive UPS
entries.summary: A UPS that passes mains to the load through a voltage-correcting stage and switches to its bidirectional inverter on failure.
description: A line-interactive UPS supplies the load from mains in normal operation, using an automatic voltage regulation stage, often a tapped autotransformer, to correct sags and swells. One bidirectional converter charges the battery while mains is present and inverts from the battery when mains fails, with a short transfer of a few milliseconds.

Drawings show the mains path through a voltage regulating element and a transfer switch to the output, with the bidirectional converter and battery connected alongside the output. It is common for small to medium ratings serving IT equipment and controls.

Output frequency follows the mains in normal operation, so the load is not protected from frequency variations, which matters on generator supplies. The symbol does not show the transfer time or the voltage correction range.
readingNotes: Look for a tapped transformer or regulation element in the mains path.
Expect a short transfer on mains failure.
drawingChecklist: State VA rating, transfer time and correction range.
Show battery and converter connection.
Reference generator compatibility.
entries.distinction: A line-interactive UPS corrects voltage on the mains path; an offline UPS passes mains without correction until it transfers.

entries.name: Offline standby UPS
entries.summary: A UPS that passes raw mains straight to the load and starts its inverter only when mains is lost.
description: An offline or standby UPS connects the load directly to mains through a transfer relay. A separate charger keeps the battery topped up, and the inverter starts only when mains fails, at which point the relay transfers the load. Transfer typically takes several milliseconds to around ten milliseconds.

Drawings show the mains path through a changeover contact to the output, with the charger, battery and inverter forming a parallel branch that connects to the other contact position. These units are mainly small desktop or control panel units.

The load sees mains disturbances and the transfer gap, and the inverter waveform may be stepped rather than sinusoidal. The symbol does not show waveform quality, transfer time or whether surge filtering is included.
readingNotes: The normal path has no conversion stage.
Check output waveform type for sensitive loads.
drawingChecklist: State VA rating and transfer time.
Show transfer relay, charger and inverter.
Reference output waveform.
entries.distinction: An offline UPS gives no correction until it transfers; an online UPS conditions the output continuously.

entries.name: Rotary UPS
entries.summary: A UPS built around a rotating synchronous machine with kinetic storage, often coupled to a diesel engine for long backup.
description: A rotary UPS uses a synchronous machine running continuously on the critical bus, with stored kinetic energy in a flywheel or induction coupling bridging the gap until a coupled diesel engine starts and takes over. A choke between the utility and the critical bus lets the machine condition the supply and isolate the load from network faults.

Single-line diagrams show the incoming utility feeder, a series choke, the synchronous machine with its kinetic energy module and clutch to the engine, and the critical and sometimes non-critical outputs. A bypass path around the unit is normally drawn.

The machine provides real short-circuit current, unlike a static UPS, which helps downstream protection discriminate. The symbol does not show the ride-through time to engine pickup or the choke impedance, both of which matter for design.
readingNotes: Identify the choke between the utility and critical bus.
Check engine coupling and the kinetic module.
drawingChecklist: State machine rating and ride-through time.
Show choke, engine coupling and bypass.
Reference fault current contribution.
entries.distinction: A rotary UPS uses rotating machines and kinetic storage; a static UPS uses power electronics and a battery.

entries.name: UPS maintenance bypass
entries.summary: An arrangement of interlocked switches that routes the load around a UPS so the UPS can be isolated for work.
description: A UPS maintenance bypass is a set of switches, usually input, output and bypass, that lets the load be connected directly to the bypass supply while the UPS is fully isolated. It is normally external to the UPS cabinet so that the UPS itself can be removed without disturbing the load wiring.

Single-line diagrams show the UPS between an input switch and an output switch, with a bypass switch connecting the input supply directly to the output busbar. Key interlocks or a make-before-break sequence prevent the UPS inverter from being paralleled with an unsynchronised bypass.

The symbol does not tell you the sequence of operation or whether the UPS static bypass must be engaged first. Those steps are critical and must be written on the operating label or switching instruction.
readingNotes: Identify the three switches and their interlock.
The bypass source may differ from the UPS rectifier source.
drawingChecklist: State ratings of each switch.
Show interlocks.
Reference operating sequence.
entries.distinction: A maintenance bypass is external switching around the whole UPS; the static bypass is an internal electronic path.

entries.name: Static var compensator
entries.summary: A shunt reactive power compensator built from thyristor-controlled reactors, thyristor-switched capacitors and filters.
description: A static var compensator is a shunt-connected installation that controls voltage by rapidly varying the reactive power it exchanges with the network. Its branches are typically a thyristor-controlled reactor, one or more thyristor-switched capacitors and harmonic filters, all connected to the secondary of a dedicated step-down transformer.

Single-line diagrams show the compensator transformer feeding a medium-voltage bus with each branch drawn separately, or a summary block labelled SVC with a variable capacitor-reactor symbol. It is used at transmission substations, at large industrial loads such as arc furnaces and at some renewable connection points.

Because its output is based on switched reactances, available reactive current falls with voltage, so it gives less support during deep voltage dips than a STATCOM. The symbol does not show the control slope, the branch ratings or the harmonic performance.
readingNotes: Read each branch rating to find the inductive and capacitive range.
Filters in an SVC usually also supply part of the capacitive output.
drawingChecklist: State capacitive and inductive range in Mvar.
Show transformer and branches.
Reference voltage control slope.
entries.distinction: An SVC varies switched reactances; a STATCOM uses a voltage-source converter and holds output current better at low voltage.

entries.name: Thyristor-controlled reactor
entries.summary: A shunt reactor in series with anti-parallel thyristors whose firing angle sets the reactive power absorbed.
description: A thyristor-controlled reactor is an air-core reactor in series with a pair of anti-parallel thyristor valves. Delaying the firing angle reduces the current conduction period, so the reactor absorbs a continuously adjustable amount of reactive power from zero to its full rating.

Drawings show the reactor symbol with the thyristor pair below it, usually in a delta connection with the reactor split into two halves on either side of the valve. It is the inductive branch of a static var compensator and also appears in some arc furnace compensation schemes.

Partial conduction generates harmonic currents, mainly odd orders, so the TCR is almost always accompanied by filters. The symbol does not show the filter arrangement or the valve cooling, which is a significant part of the installation.
readingNotes: The reactor is often drawn in two halves with the valve between them.
Delta connection cancels triplen harmonics under balanced conditions.
drawingChecklist: State reactor rating and firing range.
Show valve and connection.
Reference associated filters.
entries.distinction: A TCR varies its absorption continuously; a thyristor-switched reactor is only fully on or fully off.

entries.name: Thyristor-switched capacitor
entries.summary: A capacitor bank switched in or out at current zero by anti-parallel thyristors, giving fast stepwise reactive support.
description: A thyristor-switched capacitor connects a capacitor bank through anti-parallel thyristors, usually with a small series reactor to limit inrush. The thyristors switch the capacitor in at the instant when the network voltage equals the capacitor voltage, avoiding transients, and switch it out at current zero. It is either fully on or fully off.

Single-line diagrams show a capacitor, a series reactor and the thyristor pair stacked on a shunt branch. Several TSC branches may be drawn to give multiple steps of capacitive output in a static var compensator or a fast power factor correction system.

Because it switches in discrete steps, fine control comes from combining TSC branches with a TCR. The symbol does not show discharge resistors or the valve voltage rating, which must withstand twice the peak voltage when the capacitor is charged and the network reverses.
readingNotes: A small series reactor is part of the branch, not a separate filter.
Count branches to find available steps.
drawingChecklist: State capacitor Mvar per step.
Show series reactor and valve.
Reference switching logic.
entries.distinction: A TSC switches capacitors in steps without transients; a mechanically switched capacitor uses a breaker and is much slower.

entries.name: Static synchronous compensator
entries.summary: A voltage-source converter in shunt that injects or absorbs reactive current to support voltage, independent of system voltage.
description: A static synchronous compensator is a voltage-source converter connected in shunt through a reactor or transformer. By controlling the magnitude of its AC output voltage relative to the network, it supplies or absorbs reactive current. It responds within milliseconds and can maintain close to rated current even when network voltage is low.

Drawings show a converter block with a DC capacitor on its DC side, a coupling reactor or transformer, and the connection breaker. Distribution-scale units serving microgrids, wind farms and industrial plants are often drawn as a single converter block labelled STATCOM.

Many STATCOMs can also act as active filters for flicker and harmonics, or be paired with batteries for active power support. The symbol does not show overload capability or which of these functions are enabled.
readingNotes: A DC capacitor rather than a battery on the DC side marks a pure reactive compensator.
Check whether a battery is shown, which would add active power capability.
drawingChecklist: State Mvar range and response time.
Show coupling reactor or transformer.
Reference control functions enabled.
entries.distinction: A STATCOM uses a converter and keeps reactive current at low voltage; an SVC uses switched reactances whose output falls with voltage.

entries.name: Synchronous condenser
entries.summary: An unloaded synchronous machine on the network that supplies reactive power, inertia and short-circuit strength.
description: A synchronous condenser is a synchronous machine running without a prime mover, connected to the network to supply or absorb reactive power by adjusting its field current. Because it is a real rotating machine it also contributes inertia and high short-circuit current, which converter-dominated networks often lack.

Single-line diagrams draw a synchronous machine circle labelled SC or with a capacitor-like note, connected through a step-up transformer and breaker, with a starting arrangement such as a pony motor or static frequency converter. A flywheel may be shown on the shaft to add inertia.

The symbol looks like a generator but the machine exports no active power and draws a small amount to cover losses. It does not show the starting method, inertia constant or overexcitation limits, which define how much it helps during faults.
readingNotes: There is no prime mover; a pony motor or static starter is used only to bring the machine up to speed.
Check for a flywheel added to raise inertia.
drawingChecklist: State Mvar range, inertia and short-circuit contribution.
Show transformer and starting method.
Reference excitation limits.
entries.distinction: A synchronous condenser exchanges only reactive power; a synchronous generator also delivers active power from a prime mover.

entries.name: Single-tuned harmonic filter
entries.summary: A shunt series-LC branch tuned near one harmonic order to sink that harmonic current from the network.
description: A single-tuned filter is a capacitor and reactor in series, connected in shunt and tuned to resonate near one harmonic frequency, often slightly below the 5th, 7th or 11th. At that frequency it presents a low impedance and draws harmonic current away from the network, while at fundamental frequency it supplies capacitive reactive power.

Drawings show a capacitor and reactor in series on a shunt branch, labelled with the tuned order, and often several such branches for different orders. Unbalance protection for the capacitor bank and a dedicated breaker are normally shown.

A tuned filter creates a parallel resonance with the network at a frequency just below its tuning, which can amplify other harmonics. The symbol does not show the network impedance scan or detuning tolerance, so the harmonic study must accompany it.
readingNotes: Read the harmonic order label on each branch.
The filter also supplies fundamental reactive power.
drawingChecklist: State tuned order, Mvar and quality factor.
Show breaker and unbalance protection.
Reference harmonic study.
entries.distinction: A single-tuned filter targets one harmonic order; a damped high-pass filter attenuates a broad band above its corner frequency.

entries.name: Damped high-pass harmonic filter
entries.summary: A shunt filter with a resistor across its reactor, giving low impedance over a broad band of higher harmonics.
description: A damped high-pass filter adds a resistor in parallel with the reactor of a capacitor-reactor branch. Above its corner frequency the filter impedance stays low across a wide band, so it absorbs higher-order harmonics and damps resonances rather than sinking one specific order. The C-type variant adds a second capacitor to remove fundamental-frequency losses in the resistor.

Drawings show the capacitor in series with a reactor that has a resistor in parallel, sometimes with the extra capacitor of the C-type arrangement in series with the reactor. It is used beside tuned filters in static var compensators, large rectifier plants and some converter connection points.

The resistor dissipates real power, so its thermal rating is as important as the electrical values. The symbol does not show the corner frequency or the loss figure, which come from the filter design report.
readingNotes: A resistor across the reactor marks a damped filter.
An extra series capacitor indicates a C-type arrangement.
drawingChecklist: State corner frequency, Mvar and resistor rating.
Show resistor and capacitor arrangement.
Reference filter design report.
entries.distinction: A damped high-pass filter covers a band of harmonics; a single-tuned filter sinks one order and has no resistor branch.

entries.name: Active harmonic filter
entries.summary: A shunt converter that measures load harmonics and injects opposing currents to cancel them at the connection point.
description: An active harmonic filter is a shunt-connected voltage-source converter that measures load current through current transformers, calculates the harmonic content and injects equal and opposite currents. It can also correct power factor and balance load between phases. Response adapts to changing loads, so it does not need tuning to particular orders.

Single-line diagrams show a converter block with a wave or harmonic mark, connected to the switchboard bus through a breaker, with current transformers on the load side or on the supply side depending on the control method. Several modules are often paralleled.

The filter rating is in amperes of compensation current, not in kvar, and it can only cancel harmonics within that current and frequency range. The symbol does not tell you where the current transformers are, which decides whether the filter compensates the whole board or one load.
readingNotes: Find the current transformers; their position defines what is being compensated.
Ratings are given in compensating amperes.
drawingChecklist: State compensating current and harmonic range.
Show current transformer location.
Reference parallel module arrangement.
entries.distinction: An active filter cancels harmonics with a converter; a passive filter sinks them with tuned capacitors and reactors.

entries.name: Detuned capacitor bank
entries.summary: Power factor correction capacitors with series reactors that tune each step below the lowest significant harmonic.
description: A detuned capacitor bank places a reactor in series with each capacitor step so that the step resonates at a frequency below the lowest significant harmonic, commonly expressed as a detuning factor such as 7 per cent, which tunes near 189 Hz on a 50 Hz network. This prevents the bank from forming a parallel resonance that would amplify 5th harmonic currents from converters.

Single-line diagrams show several capacitor steps, each with a series reactor and a switching contactor or thyristor switch, controlled by a power factor regulator using a current transformer on the incoming supply. The detuning factor is noted on the bank.

The series reactor raises the voltage across the capacitors above network voltage, so the capacitors must be rated accordingly. The symbol does not show that voltage rise, the reactor thermal rating or the regulator settings.
readingNotes: Read the detuning factor, usually given as a percentage.
Capacitor voltage rating should exceed network voltage.
drawingChecklist: State kvar per step and detuning factor.
Show reactors, switching and regulator CT.
Reference capacitor voltage rating.
entries.distinction: A detuned bank avoids resonance and absorbs little harmonic current; a tuned filter is designed to sink harmonic current.

entries.name: Dynamic voltage restorer
entries.summary: A series converter that injects a corrective voltage through a transformer to ride a sensitive load through voltage sags.
description: A dynamic voltage restorer is connected in series between the supply and a sensitive load through an injection transformer. When the supply voltage sags, a converter fed from a DC store or from the supply itself injects the missing voltage so the load sees an almost constant voltage, typically for sags lasting up to a few seconds.

Single-line diagrams show an injection transformer with its primary in series with the feeder, its secondary connected to a converter, and a DC capacitor or storage element. A bypass switch around the injection transformer allows the device to be taken out of service.

A DVR corrects sags but does not supply the load during a full outage, unlike a UPS. The symbol does not show the maximum sag depth or duration it can correct, which depends on the stored energy and converter rating.
readingNotes: The series transformer, not a shunt connection, identifies a DVR.
Check the bypass arrangement for maintenance.
drawingChecklist: State load rating, sag depth and duration corrected.
Show injection transformer and bypass.
Reference energy store.
entries.distinction: A DVR injects series voltage for sags; a STATCOM injects shunt current to support bus voltage.

entries.name: Point of common coupling
entries.summary: A marker on a single-line diagram identifying where a customer installation or microgrid meets the public network.
description: The point of common coupling is the location on the network nearest to the installation where other customers are, or could be, connected. Harmonic, flicker and voltage limits in connection agreements are assessed at this point, and microgrid islanding decisions are often defined relative to it.

Drawings mark the point with a dot, circle, flag or label PCC on the busbar or cable, often together with the ownership boundary and the revenue meter. A microgrid may show both a PCC with the utility and internal points of connection for each source.

The marker carries no electrical function itself. It does not tell you the ownership boundary, which can differ from the PCC, or the fault level at that point, which must be stated for compliance assessments.
readingNotes: Do not assume the PCC and the ownership boundary coincide.
Power quality limits are assessed here.
drawingChecklist: State voltage level and fault level at the PCC.
Show the ownership boundary separately.
Reference connection agreement limits.
entries.distinction: A PCC marks an assessment point; a utility grid connection symbol represents the supply itself.

entries.name: Utility grid connection
entries.summary: The symbol for the external utility network as a supply source at the top of a single-line diagram.
description: The utility grid connection symbol represents the public supply network as seen from the installation. It is drawn at the top or edge of a single-line diagram to show where power enters, and in a microgrid it is one of several sources, typically the reference source when the microgrid is grid-connected.

Common forms include a lattice tower glyph, a circle with a sine wave, a set of arrows into the busbar or a box labelled UTILITY or GRID. Voltage, prospective fault level and earthing system of the supply are written beside it.

The symbol does not show the network operator protection or reclose behaviour, which affects whether downstream generation must disconnect quickly. Those details come from the connection agreement and are usually noted on the drawing.
readingNotes: Read the fault level and X/R ratio noted beside the source.
The earthing system of the supply affects downstream design.
drawingChecklist: State voltage, fault level and earthing system.
Show incoming protection and metering.
Reference connection agreement.
entries.distinction: A utility connection represents the external network; a grid equivalent source is a study model with defined impedance.

entries.name: Grid equivalent source
entries.summary: A voltage source behind an impedance used in study diagrams to represent the external network at a defined fault level.
description: A grid equivalent source represents the upstream network in load flow, short circuit and stability studies as an ideal voltage source behind an impedance. The impedance is calculated from the declared fault level and X/R ratio at the connection point, often with separate maximum and minimum cases.

Study single-line diagrams draw it as a circle with a sine wave followed by an impedance element, labelled with the fault level in MVA or kA and the X/R ratio. Microgrid studies use it to test both strong and weak network conditions before islanding scenarios are modelled.

The equivalent is only valid near the declared fault level; it cannot represent upstream dynamics such as voltage control or frequency response unless additional models are attached. The symbol does not tell you which study case it belongs to.
readingNotes: Read both the fault level and X/R ratio.
Check whether the drawing shows maximum or minimum fault case.
drawingChecklist: State fault level, X/R ratio and voltage.
Show the impedance element.
Reference study case.

entries.name: Microgrid interconnection switch
entries.summary: The switching device that separates a microgrid from the utility for islanding and reconnects it after synchronising.
description: The microgrid interconnection switch is the breaker or switch at the boundary with the utility that opens to island the microgrid and closes to reconnect it. Its control is tied to interface protection, which detects loss of mains, and to the microgrid controller, which manages planned islanding and resynchronisation.

Single-line diagrams show a circuit breaker at the point of common coupling with protection functions listed beside it, commonly under and over voltage, under and over frequency, rate of change of frequency, directional power and synchronism check. A label such as MIS or island breaker identifies its role.

The breaker itself is an ordinary device; its function comes from the protection and control logic. The symbol does not show whether reconnection is automatic, how long it waits or whether a seamless transition is possible.
readingNotes: Read the protection functions listed beside the breaker.
Synchronism check must supervise closing.
drawingChecklist: State interface protection functions and settings source.
Show synchronism check and controller link.
Reference islanding and reconnection logic.

entries.name: Resistive load bank
entries.summary: A bank of switched resistive elements used to apply a controllable test load to generators, UPS or battery systems.
description: A resistive load bank is a set of resistor elements, switched in steps and cooled by fans, used to load a generator, UPS or battery system for commissioning and maintenance tests. Permanent load banks are also installed to keep diesel engines above minimum load when site demand is low.

Drawings show a resistor symbol or a group of resistors with step switches, connected through a breaker to the bus being tested. Permanently installed banks have a control link to the genset or microgrid controller, while portable banks connect through a temporary test connection point.

A resistive bank loads at unity power factor only, so it does not test a generator at its rated kVA when the rated power factor is below one. The symbol does not show step sizes or fan supply, both needed for test planning.
readingNotes: A purely resistive bank tests kW, not kVA.
Look for a dedicated test connection point.
drawingChecklist: State kW rating and step sizes.
Show breaker and fan supply.
Reference control interface.

entries.name: Resistive-reactive load bank
entries.summary: A test load bank combining resistive and inductive steps to load a generator at its rated power factor.
description: A resistive-reactive load bank adds inductive reactor steps to resistive elements so that a generator can be tested at its full rated kVA and rated power factor, typically 0.8 lagging. This exercises the alternator excitation, voltage regulator and transformer heating in a way a resistive bank cannot.
Drawings show resistor and reactor groups in parallel, each with step switching, connected through a breaker. The power factor range and the kW and kvar totals are written beside the symbol.

Reactive load banks are heavier and more costly, so they are mainly used for commissioning large sets and paralleling tests. The symbol does not show the switching sequence or the instrumentation used to record test results.

entries.name: Neutral earthing resistor
entries.summary: A resistor between a transformer or generator neutral and earth that limits earth-fault current to a set value.
description: A neutral earthing resistor connects the star point of a transformer or generator to earth through a defined resistance. It limits earth-fault current, typically to tens or hundreds of amperes on medium-voltage systems and a few amperes on high-resistance earthed low-voltage systems, reducing damage and arc energy while keeping enough current for protection to detect.

Drawings show a resistor between the neutral of a star winding and the earth symbol, often with a current transformer in the neutral lead for earth-fault protection and sometimes a disconnector. The resistor current and time rating, such as 400 A for 10 seconds, are written beside it.

The symbol does not show the resistor's monitoring, which some designs use to detect an open resistor. It also does not show whether generator and transformer neutrals are earthed at the same time, which affects fault current and circulating harmonic currents.
readingNotes: Read the current and time rating together.
A neutral CT normally feeds earth-fault protection.
drawingChecklist: State resistance, current and time rating.
Show neutral CT and disconnector.
Reference earth-fault protection settings.
entries.distinction: A neutral earthing resistor limits fault current resistively; an arc suppression coil compensates capacitive fault current with inductance.

entries.name: Arc suppression coil
entries.summary: An adjustable reactor between neutral and earth tuned to cancel the network capacitive earth-fault current.
description: An arc suppression coil is a reactor connected between the system neutral and earth, tuned so that its inductive current balances the capacitive current that flows during a single phase-to-earth fault. The residual fault current becomes very small, so transient arcing faults often self-extinguish and the network can keep running with a sustained earth fault.

Drawings show an inductor with an adjustment arrow between a transformer or earthing transformer neutral and earth, often with a parallel resistor switched in briefly to help fault location. Automatic tuning controllers and neutral voltage measurement are drawn alongside.

Resonant earthing needs dedicated earth-fault detection, such as transient or admittance-based protection, because fault current is too small for simple overcurrent relays. The symbol does not show the tuning range or the detection method.
readingNotes: An adjustment arrow on the reactor shows tuning capability.
Look for a parallel resistor used for fault location.
drawingChecklist: State tuning range in amperes.
Show earthing transformer and resistor.
Reference earth-fault detection method.
entries.distinction: An arc suppression coil cancels capacitive fault current; a neutral earthing resistor limits fault current but does not cancel it.

entries.name: Microgrid controller
entries.summary: The supervisory controller that dispatches sources, storage and loads and manages islanding and reconnection of a microgrid.
description: A microgrid controller coordinates the sources, storage and controllable loads within a microgrid. It sets operating points for inverters and gensets, maintains spinning reserve, sheds and restores load, and manages transitions between grid-connected and islanded operation, including black start and resynchronisation.

On single-line diagrams it is shown as a control block, often at the side of the drawing, with dashed communication lines to each controlled breaker, inverter, genset controller and meter. Architecture drawings show it in more detail, including the communication protocols and the hierarchy of controllers below it.

The block does not reveal how fast the controller acts or which functions run locally in device controllers instead. Protection must never rely on the supervisory controller alone, so check that each device has its own protection independent of the communication link.
readingNotes: Dashed lines from the block are signal or communication links, not power paths.
Identify which functions remain local if communication fails.
drawingChecklist: List controlled devices and signals.
Show communication links and protocols.
Reference operating modes and fallback behaviour.
entries.distinction: A microgrid controller supervises the whole system; a genset or inverter controller controls one device.

entries.name: Genset controller
entries.summary: The device controller that starts, protects and synchronises a generating set and controls its breaker.
description: A genset controller starts and stops the engine, monitors engine sensors, provides generator protection functions and, in paralleling versions, synchronises the set and shares load with other sources. Automatic mains failure versions also monitor the utility supply and control the changeover.

Single-line diagrams draw it as a block beside the generator with measurement inputs from generator CTs and VTs, a breaker close and trip connection and a communication link to the microgrid or power management controller. The protection functions it provides are often listed by device number.

The block does not tell you whether it provides certified utility interface protection or only generator protection. It also does not show the governor and regulator interface, which may be analogue, digital or a communication link to the engine control unit.
readingNotes: Read the listed protection functions; they may not include interface protection.
Check breaker control and synchronising connections.
drawingChecklist: List protection and control functions.
Show measurement and breaker connections.
Reference governor and regulator interface.
entries.distinction: A genset controller handles one set; a microgrid controller coordinates many sources.

facts.value: Breaker control, governor and AVR commands

entries.name: Power plant controller
entries.summary: The plant-level controller that measures at the connection point and sets inverter or turbine outputs to meet grid requirements.
description: A power plant controller measures voltage, current, active and reactive power at the plant connection point and adjusts setpoints of all inverters or turbines to meet the network operator's requirements. Typical functions include active power limits, ramp rates, frequency response, voltage or reactive power control and power factor control.

Drawings show a control block with measurement inputs from the connection point CTs and VTs, a communication network to each inverter or turbine, and a link to the network operator's control system. A meter at the point of connection is usually the measurement source.

The controller's response speed is slower than the inverter internal controls, so fast events are still handled by the devices themselves. The symbol does not show control modes, settings or the response time agreed with the network operator.
readingNotes: Measurement comes from the connection point, not individual inverters.
Communication dashed lines show the setpoint path.
drawingChecklist: List control modes and the measurement point.
Show communication to each unit.
Reference agreed performance settings.
entries.distinction: A power plant controller manages one generating plant at its connection point; a microgrid controller also manages loads and islanding.

facts.value: P, Q, voltage, ramp, frequency response

entries.name: Dump load controller
entries.summary: A controller that diverts surplus generation into a resistive dump load to hold frequency or voltage in a small isolated system.
description: A dump load controller keeps a small isolated system in balance by diverting surplus power into a resistive load, usually water or air heaters. In micro hydro systems it holds frequency constant by keeping total generator load fixed, and in small wind or battery systems it protects the battery from overcharge by dumping excess energy.

Drawings show a controller block, often with a thyristor or transistor switch symbol, connected between the bus and a resistor bank labelled dump or ballast load. A frequency or voltage sensing connection to the bus is included.
The dump load must be rated to absorb the full generator output if all consumer loads disconnect. The symbol does not show that rating or the heat rejection arrangement, both important for safety.
readingNotes: The resistor bank is a control element, not a consumer load.
Check the sensing quantity: frequency for hydro, voltage for battery systems.
drawingChecklist: State dump load rating against generator rating.
Show sensing and switching element.
Reference heat rejection.
entries.distinction: A dump load controller diverts surplus energy continuously; a load bank is a test load used temporarily.

facts.label: Typical use
facts.value: Micro hydro, small wind, off-grid systems

entries.name: Split-phase inverter
entries.summary: An inverter with two 180-degree displaced outputs and a neutral, supplying 120/240 V split-phase installations.
description: A split-phase inverter produces two AC outputs 180 degrees apart with a shared neutral, giving 120 V from each line to neutral and 240 V between lines. This matches North American residential and small commercial supplies, so the inverter can feed a standard load centre in off-grid or backup systems.

Drawings show the inverter block with three AC output conductors, L1, L2 and N, often with an internal or external autotransformer that balances unequal loads on the two halves. Neutral-earth bonding relays and the generator or grid input are drawn as for other inverter-chargers.

Unequal loading on L1 and L2 must be handled by the inverter or an autotransformer; otherwise one half can overload while the total rating appears adequate. The symbol does not show the per-leg current rating or the bonding arrangement.
readingNotes: Read the per-leg rating as well as the total rating.
Check for an autotransformer used for load balancing.
drawingChecklist: State total and per-leg ratings.
Show L1, L2, N and bonding.
Reference load balance between legs.
entries.distinction: A split-phase inverter produces two antiphase legs; a three-phase inverter produces three legs 120 degrees apart.

facts.label: Voltages
facts.value: 120 V line to neutral, 240 V line to line

entries.name: IEC pushbutton contact: mushroom head normally open momentary
aliases: pushbutton contact Mushroom Head Normally Open Momentary
entries.summary: Pushbutton contact form: Mushroom Head Normally Open Momentary.
description: A pushbutton translates a person pressing an operator into a change of electrical contact state. The operator form and the contact state are separate pieces of information, so a mushroom head can operate either a normally-open or a normally-closed contact. This entry identifies the mushroom head normally open momentary form in the publisher's IEC-context family.

On a machine control sheet, this form lets the reader distinguish the physical button action from the contact used by the controller. Link every contact block to the same operator tag, including a separate indication lamp when fitted. The normally-open designation starts with a non-conducting output or open contact in the documented reference condition; operation changes that state. The momentary operator returns after it is released; the control logic must not assume that its mechanical state remains latched.

The head shape and contact drawing do not establish a safety category, contact rating or emergency-stop suitability. Direct opening, reset behaviour and the selected assembly must be confirmed from its documentation.
readingNotes: The normally-open designation starts with a non-conducting output or open contact in the documented reference condition; operation changes that state.

entries.name: IEC pushbutton contact: normally open push button recessed
aliases: pushbutton contact Normally Open Push Button Recessed
entries.summary: Pushbutton contact form: Normally Open Push Button Recessed.
description: A pushbutton translates a person pressing an operator into a change of electrical contact state. The operator form and the contact state are separate pieces of information, so a mushroom head can operate either a normally-open or a normally-closed contact. This entry identifies the normally open push button recessed form in the publisher's IEC-context family.

On a machine control sheet, this form lets the reader distinguish the physical button action from the contact used by the controller. Link every contact block to the same operator tag, including a separate indication lamp when fitted. The normally-open designation starts with a non-conducting output or open contact in the documented reference condition; operation changes that state. The recessed operator is represented as protected by its surrounding profile, which helps distinguish it from a projecting button in the operator schedule.

The head shape and contact drawing do not establish a safety category, contact rating or emergency-stop suitability. Direct opening, reset behaviour and the selected assembly must be confirmed from its documentation.

entries.name: IEC selector-switch contact: 2 position maintain, normally closed
aliases: selector-switch contact 2 Position Maintain, Normally Closed
entries.summary: Selector-switch contact form: 2 Position Maintain, Normally Closed.
description: A rotary selector has discrete handle positions and one or more contact blocks driven by its mechanism. A contact shown as normally open or normally closed describes the stated reference position; it does not give the whole switching table across the remaining positions. This entry identifies the 2 position maintain, normally closed form in the publisher's IEC-context family.

For a local/off/remote selector, prepare a contact-versus-position chart alongside the schematic. The chart tells the installer which input is active at each handle setting, while spring-return, maintained and key-operated marks explain how the operator reaches or leaves that setting. The normally-closed designation starts with a conducting output or closed contact in the documented reference condition; operation changes that state.

A vendor neutral-position number must be read with that vendor form and the project legend. It does not automatically establish a key-removal position, a contact overlap or an off state. Those details need their own table or equipment reference.

The normally-open designation starts with a non-conducting output or open contact in the documented reference condition; operation changes that state. Keep the publisher's neutral 1 designation beside its contact table; do not infer the complete position sequence from that number.

A contact shown as normally open or normally closed describes the stated reference position; it does not give the whole switching table across the remaining positions. This entry identifies the 4 stable positions key selector normally closed-rotating cw form in the publisher's IEC-context family.

For a local/off/remote selector, prepare a contact-versus-position chart alongside the schematic. The chart tells the installer which input is active at each handle setting, while spring-return, maintained and key-operated marks explain how the operator reaches or leaves that setting. The normally-closed designation starts with a conducting output or closed contact in the documented reference condition; operation changes that state. The selected key-selector form restricts the documented operating direction to clockwise movement, which must agree with the front-panel position labels.

A vendor neutral-position number must be read with that vendor form and the project legend. It does not automatically establish a key-removal position, a contact overlap or an off state. Those details need their own table or equipment reference.

entries.name: IEC fused switching form: 1 phase disconnect with fuse
aliases: fused switching form 1 Phase Disconnect with Fuse
entries.summary: Fused switching form form: 1 Phase Disconnect with Fuse.
description: A fused switching form identifies a switch and a fuse within the documented arrangement. Switching load current, providing isolation and interrupting a fault are separate capabilities, and the drawing must show which element performs each role. This entry identifies the 1 phase disconnect with fuse form in the publisher's IEC-context family.

An outgoing panel feeder can show a fused switch with its operating handle and fuse reference. Keep the switching tag linked to the fuse schedule so replacement protection and the intended switching duty can be checked together.

The family name does not establish a device utilization category or prove that a fuse carrier may be moved under load. Use the selected assembly documentation for load operation, isolation indication, fuse class and any interlocks.

entries.name: IEC motor-starter form: motor starter coil
entries.summary: Motor-starter form form: Motor Starter Coil.
description: A motor starter uses an operating coil and power contacts to control the motor feeder. The coil belongs to the control circuit; the main contacts carry motor current. Auxiliary contacts report or interlock operation but do not replace the main poles. This entry identifies the motor starter coil form in the publisher's IEC-context family.

A start command can energise the starter coil while the linked main poles connect the motor supply. Reuse the same device tag on the coil and contacts, then cross-reference overload and short-circuit protection as distinct parts of the feeder.

The contact illustration is a functional view of one pole, not a complete motor starter or a proof of fault protection. Coil voltage, duty, overload coordination and the number of linked poles come from the chosen equipment and design.

entries.name: IEC mechanical position-switch contact: limit switch, roller normally closed
aliases: mechanical position-switch contact Limit Switch, Roller Normally Closed
entries.summary: Mechanical position-switch contact form: Limit Switch, Roller Normally Closed.
description: A mechanically operated position switch changes its contact state when travel, a cam or a lever reaches the documented operating condition. The actuator mark explains how movement reaches the switch; the electrical contact still has to be read in its stated unoperated position. This entry identifies the limit switch, roller normally closed form in the publisher's IEC-context family.

A moving carriage may operate the switch near the end of travel, or an operator may move a multidirectional lever. Identify the actual direction or target position on the drawing and connect the switch tag to the corresponding mechanical detail. The normally-closed designation starts with a conducting output or closed contact in the documented reference condition; operation changes that state.

Detents retain an operating position and are different from a spring-return mechanism. The schematic does not supply operating travel, overtravel, contact force or a safety performance level; use the selected switch data for those properties.

description: An ultrasonic proximity sensor uses sound above the audible range to detect a target or measure a return echo. This entry identifies the normally open 3 wire with connector form in the publisher's IEC-context family.

The normally-open designation starts with a non-conducting output or open contact in the documented reference condition; operation changes that state. The three-wire form distinguishes supply, return and switching output. Confirm sourcing or sinking operation from the actual sensor circuit before connecting it to an input.

entries.summary: Two-wire PLC point form: IN, 1st Point, 2 Wires.
description: A two-wire PLC point form shows two terminal connections associated with a controller input or output point. The symbol is an interface reference, and the module data must establish whether the connection is digital, analogue, isolated or part of a shared common group. This entry identifies the in, 1st point, 2 wires form in the publisher's IEC-context family.

When tracing a field device to a PLC terminal strip, identify the rack, module, channel and both terminal numbers. Follow the common or return conductor as carefully as the signal conductor so a technician can reconcile the schematic with the module wiring sheet. The two-connection interface must be read with the load and supply arrangement. Leakage current and minimum load can matter where a powered device is connected in series with an input.

Two drawn wires do not prove that the field device is loop-powered or that a point can supply current. Electrical type, polarity, common grouping and internal protection depend on the selected module and cannot be inferred from the outline.

description: This reference locates neutral link, closed in Autodesk's IEEE-oriented fuses family. Rules on whether the neutral may be separately disconnected differ between earthing schemes. Do not read the holder as a fuse. A closed neutral link is a removable connection; a neutral fuse would be a protective device and is generally not permitted. entries.name: ANSI/IEEE Minimum-impedance measuring relay form
entries.summary: IEEE-library form of minimum-impedance measuring relay: measuring relay that compares voltage with current and operates when the apparent impedance falls below a set value.
description: This reference locates minimum-impedance measuring relay in Autodesk's IEEE-oriented miscellaneous relays family. A minimum-impedance relay divides measured voltage by measured current and operates when the result falls below its setting, indicating a fault close enough to fall inside its reach. It is used as generator and transformer backup protection and is the basic idea behind distance protection. The public library uses HCR1F41 for its horizontal representation; this is a vendor block name, not an IEEE standards symbol number.

Trace the measured quantity or initiating control signal separately from the output contacts. The device tag links the sensing or operating element to the controlled circuit; settings, reset behaviour and the actual terminal arrangement belong in the selected equipment documentation.

The relay needs both CT and VT inputs, so the symbol should always be read with both connections. It does not show the characteristic shape on the impedance plane, any directional element, or the loss-of-voltage blocking needed to avoid operation when the VT supply fails. Confirm both voltage and current inputs are shown. A minimum-impedance relay uses voltage and current together; an overcurrent relay uses current alone. The linked functional counterpart explains the same operating role in its own drawing context; agreement of every detailed convention mark is not asserted.
readingNotes: Confirm both voltage and current inputs are shown.
Check for VT fuse-failure blocking.
drawingChecklist: Show CT and VT inputs
State reach and delay
Reference blocking logic
entries.distinction: A minimum-impedance relay uses voltage and current together; an overcurrent relay uses current alone.

entries.name: ANSI/IEEE Insulation monitoring relay form
entries.summary: IEEE-library form of insulation monitoring relay: relay that continuously checks insulation resistance of an unearthed (IT) system to earth and alarms on a first fault.
description: This reference locates insulation monitoring relay in Autodesk's IEEE-oriented miscellaneous relays family. An insulation monitoring relay is connected between the conductors of an unearthed (IT) system and earth, and injects a measuring signal to determine insulation resistance. It warns when insulation falls below its setting so a first fault can be located before a second fault causes a trip. The public library uses HCR1F44 for its horizontal representation; this is a vendor block name, not an IEEE standards symbol number.

Trace the measured quantity or initiating control signal separately from the output contacts. The device tag links the sensing or operating element to the controlled circuit; settings, reset behaviour and the actual terminal arrangement belong in the selected equipment documentation.

The symbol shows the device and its connections but not the measuring method, which matters on systems with drives or large DC components. Only one insulation monitor should normally be active on a galvanically connected system, so the drawing should show any disconnection or interlock between parallel systems. Check that only one monitor is active on each connected IT system. An insulation monitoring relay measures insulation resistance of an unearthed system; a residual current monitor measures leakage current in an earthed system. The linked functional counterpart explains the same operating role in its own drawing context; agreement of every detailed convention mark is not asserted.
readingNotes: Check that only one monitor is active on each connected IT system.
Identify alarm outputs and test button wiring.
drawingChecklist: Show system and earth connections
State alarm thresholds
Reference interlock between parallel monitors
entries.distinction: An insulation monitoring relay measures insulation resistance of an unearthed system; a residual current monitor measures leakage current in an earthed system.

An emergency-stop station component provides part of a machine stopping interface. Its mechanical placement does not establish the safety performance of the complete stopping circuit.

For example, in a machine installation with a clearly accessible stop station, use the ESL-SSL-232018-AS reference to coordinate operator approach, operating head and rear contact wiring. Show the neighbouring equipment and the connection route so the installer can understand the intended arrangement.

Use the reviewed native drawing identified as Pushbuttons Switches Indicators/EStop Station Pushbuttons/ESL-SSL-232018-AS.dwg for the exact physical details. Locate the named file in its original manufacturer archive. Manufacturer drawing previews are shown only when an exact approved source is available. Any illustrative 3D view is a separate concept and is not to scale; use the selected manufacturer documents for dimensions, ratings and installation details.
readingNotes: Keep operator approach, operating head and rear contact wiring visible in the layout.

entries.summary: PX-312 analogue input module arrangement: mounting, interface and service-space coordination.
description: PX-312 is the drawing identifier for analogue input module in AutomationDirect's Protos X Field I/O collection. An analogue input module brings continuously varying sensor information into a controller. Its physical connectors and mounting arrangement are different questions from the signal range configured in the control program.

For example, in a process-control panel receiving transmitter signals, use the PX-312 reference to coordinate field-signal terminals, module removal and the controller connection. Show the neighbouring equipment and the connection route so the installer can understand the intended arrangement.

Use the reviewed native drawing identified as Other PLC Products/Protos X IO/PX-312.dwg for the exact physical details. Locate the named file in its original manufacturer archive. Manufacturer drawing previews are shown only when an exact approved source is available. Any illustrative 3D view is a separate concept and is not to scale; use the selected manufacturer documents for dimensions, ratings and installation details.
readingNotes: Keep field-signal terminals, module removal and the controller connection visible in the layout.

entries.name: Breaker shunt-trip coil

description: Uses an externally supplied electrical pulse to release the breaker opening mechanism. A trip circuit carries an opening request from a control or protection device to the breaker operating mechanism. The opening command, the coil supply and the evidence that the breaker opened are separate parts of the drawing.

In a switchgear incomer panel, a protection relay requests opening and an auxiliary contact reports the resulting breaker position. entries.name: Control-power automatic source selection
entries.summary: Selects the documented auxiliary source according to its availability inputs.
description: Selects the documented auxiliary source according to its availability inputs. Control power supplies the command, protection and indication equipment associated with a switchgear assembly. The drawing must distinguish the source, each distribution branch and the functions lost if that branch fails.

In a switchgear lineup, separate protected branches may feed trip coils, closing coils and protection electronics. Their alarm contacts help the station controller identify which operating capability is unavailable. For this reference, the drawing identifies “Auxiliary-source health” at the input and “Selected control-power source” at the output. Selection logic must not unintentionally parallel sources.

Follow the actual positive, negative or neutral returns and the protective device on each branch. A healthy voltage indication does not establish that every downstream path can deliver its required operating current. The functional block is an independent explanation of this named application. Equipment-specific ratings, terminal connections and operating conditions must be established in the project documentation.

entries.name: Transformer cooling stage-two request
aliases: substations Transformer regulation and cooling control
entries.summary: Requests the next defined cooling group when the selected control condition is reached.
description: Requests the next defined cooling group when the selected control condition is reached. Transformer regulation changes the selected winding connection to influence voltage, while cooling control manages the installed fans and pumps. Commands, mechanical position and measured results belong to different parts of the diagram.

In a substation, a voltage regulator can request a tap change and check the resulting tap-position feedback. A separate controller stages cooling equipment according to the transformer manufacturer's defined conditions. For this reference, the drawing identifies “Additional cooling demand” at the input and “Second cooling-group command” at the output. A stage number does not establish a thermal rating.

Keep tap-change permission, limit contacts, movement indication and measured voltage distinct. Actual tap positions, time delays, cooling ratings and allowable parallel operation require the selected transformer control design. The functional block is an independent explanation of this named application. Equipment-specific ratings, terminal connections and operating conditions must be established in the project documentation.

aliases: substations Station battery and charger distribution
entries.summary: Identifies the charger operating interface that maintains the battery at its specified standby charge condition.
description: Identifies the charger operating interface that maintains the battery at its specified standby charge condition. A station battery system supplies protection, control and other assigned DC loads through a documented charger and distribution arrangement. Charger output, battery contribution and load distribution are related but separately monitored paths.

In a substation control building, the battery can support breaker trip circuits while the charger AC supply is unavailable. Supervision must identify whether the charger, battery or a downstream feeder is affected. For this reference, the drawing identifies “Charger control and battery condition” at the input and “Float-charge operating state” at the output. Charge settings depend on battery chemistry and equipment.

entries.name: Microgrid bus-section connectivity tracker
aliases: microgrids Microgrid topology and earthing coordination
entries.summary: Determines the declared connectivity of named bus sections from their assigned switching states.
description: Determines the declared connectivity of named bus sections from their assigned switching states. Microgrid topology control tracks which sources and load sections are electrically connected. The same physical installation can form several islands, so source roles, measurement boundaries and earthing interfaces must follow the established configuration.

In a microgrid with sectionalized buses, the controller can associate each connected source and load group with its current island. A mode-dependent neutral or protection interface needs its own independently validated design. For this reference, the drawing identifies “Bus-switch position information” at the input and “Bus connectivity map” at the output. Invalid positions require defined treatment.

Keep measured switch positions, logical island assignment and any earthing command separate.
